description: KatLang is a domain-specific programming language for calculations. This package provides the core parser, evaluator, and semantic model.
releaseNotes: Migrates KatLang's numeric core from System.Decimal to IEEE 754 System.Numerics.Decimal128 (.NET 11): numbers carry 34 significant decimal digits with an exponent range of about ±6144, literals parse directly into Decimal128, and every math function (trig, logarithms, roots, powers) computes in Decimal128 natively — the former double round-trip and its 15-significant-digit result normalization are removed, so transcendental results such as Math.Sin(1) now retain full precision and large trigonometric arguments are computed directly in Decimal128 without conversion through binary64/double. Math.Pi is Decimal128's correctly rounded 34-digit constant; the former Math.E / e constant surface is replaced by Math.Exp(x) / exp(x), which delegates directly to Decimal128.Exp. Division/modulo by a zero-valued divisor and zero raised to a negative integer power remain errors; all other numerics follow IEEE 754 — overflow saturates to an infinity (the NumericOverflow error kind is removed), domain violations produce NaN, and NaN, ±Infinity, and -0 are ordinary values (ordering comparisons with NaN are false; structural equality, distinct, and contains treat NaN as one value). Public API types that exposed decimal (Result.Atom, atom projections, RunResult.Success.Atoms, EvaluateToAtoms, RunFlat, Token.NumValue, Expr.Num, Pattern.LitInt, BoundedOutputWriter.AppendAtom) now expose Decimal128; this is an intentional breaking change with no compatibility mode. Math.RandomInt now draws uniformly in the integer domain via rejection sampling and requires whole-number bounds within ±1e34 (the exactly-representable consecutive-integer domain); range bounds are validated identically on the synchronous and asynchronous evaluation paths; and host-built literal patterns (Pattern.LitInt) match by the same structural numeric equality as ==, so a NaN literal pattern matches a NaN value. Editor-facing Math metadata now uses authoritative descriptor parameter names (including radians, value/digits, value/base, and atan2's y/x order), and PropertyInfo.AliasTarget exposes the canonical qualified target and display signature only for resolved predefined aliases.
